before: is asks whether an object has a particular type or one of its subclasses, returning Bool. as? attempts a safe downcast and returns an optional reference. A successful cast gives access to subclass members; a failed cast produces nil rather than a crash. Neither operation creates a replacement object.

entry as? BookEntry returns BookEntry?. if let binds book only on success, so book.pages is safe there. BookEntry(pages:) initializes its stored Int. String(book.pages) converts that integer to decimal text, and + joins it to the label. This is different from a forced as! cast, which this lesson does not use. Entry() creates a plain base-class instance with no input fields. An Entry reference can hold either kind of object.

Keep the two class declarations and implement describe(_:) so BookEntry values produce "pages=" followed by their page count; other Entry objects produce "other". Use a safe check rather than a forced cast. Optional local practice: choose one more input, predict the outcome, then run it. The checks observe the stated values and effects; they do not require one exact implementation spelling.
after: An Entry can hold different kinds of objects. A BookEntry has a pages property that a plain Entry does not. Check the kind of object before trying to read pages.

A cast lets you use a value as a more specific type. as? BookEntry succeeds when the object is a BookEntry or one of its subclasses. It returns nil if the check fails. if let gives book a value only when the cast succeeds.
A successful cast gives access to the same object. It does not copy it or change its class. as? makes failure safe by returning nil. A forced as! cast can crash when the type is wrong.
Keep Entry and BookEntry. Complete describe(_:) so books return pages= followed by their page count. Return other for other entries. Use a safe cast before reading pages.

before.question: Does a successful as? BookEntry cast duplicate the object?
choices: It changes the class of the original object
Yes; it copies all fields into a new instance
No; it provides an optional reference to the same object
before.explanation: The cast checks the existing object’s type. Success changes what members the reference can access, not the object’s identity.

after.question: Does a successful as? BookEntry cast make a copy of the object?
choices: Yes, it creates a new object
No, it gives access to the same object
after.explanation: The cast checks the existing object's type. It does not create another object.
